title: 2010 AMC 8 Problem 18
statement: A decorative window is made up of a rectangle with semicircles on either end. The ratio of \(AD\) to \(AB\) is \(3:2,\) and \(AB=30\) inches. What is the ratio of the area of the rectangle to the combined areas of the semicircles?

solutions.text:
Combining the semicircles would make a circle of diameter \(d=30.\) This would make the radius equal to \( \dfrac{d}{2}.\) Therefore, the combined area of the semicircles is \[(\dfrac{d}{2})^2 \cdot \pi = \dfrac{\pi d^2}{4}.\]

Side \(AD = \dfrac 32 d\) because \(AD:AB=3:2\) and \(AB=d.\) The area of the rectangle is therefore \( \dfrac 32 d^2.\) The ratio of the area of the rectangle to the area of the semicircles is \(\dfrac{\dfrac 32 d^2}{\dfrac{\pi d^2}{4}} = \dfrac{6}{\pi}.\)

Thus, the answer is C .
hints: Use the ratio \(AD:AB=3:2\) to express the rectangle height in terms of \(AB\).
The two semicircles combine to one full circle.
